est_error_at_start_pose_m.source: /amcl_pose (AMCL (nav2_amcl) over /scan) paired with /ground_truth/odom by header stamp within 50 ms, truth mapped to map by apartment_frames.yaml copied verbatim into env.json
est_error_at_start_pose_m.definition: mean |estimate - truth| while the robot is at its start pose and rotating in place: from the first /amcl_pose whose covariance trace is below 0.25 to goal acceptance, excluding any pair whose truth position has already moved more than 0.05 m from the truth position at acceptance. The guard is applied to the TRUTH half of each pair; within the 50 ms pairing window the body can travel at most 0.023 m, so the bound actually enforced on the estimate half is 0.05 + 0.023 m. It is map error plus world->map alignment error AT THAT ONE POSE, measured, and it is the scale against which in-mission estimate error should be read. est_status_flags.source: none (the profile names no uncertainty topic)

localization_converged_sim_s.definition: first /amcl_pose whose covariance trace is below 0.25, minus the first /initialpose stamp. AMCL updates its filter on MOTION, so the runner rotates the robot in place while waiting; this measures that wait

collision_count.definition: /bumper messages with a non-empty contacts list inside the window, debounced at 0.5 s sim per colliding pair (gz reports a contact every physics step while two bodies touch); 0 message(s) recorded. stopped_time_s.definition: sim seconds inside the window with |linear.x| < 0.01 and |angular.z| < 0.01, zero-order hold on the bag log time (sim), the last command held to the terminal stamp

mission_result.definition: the action status of THIS goal, by UUID, as the server reported it. NavigateToPose's result payload is std_msgs/Empty, so the GoalStatus code is the only verbatim outcome the action offers

recoveries.definition: max number_of_recoveries across NavigateToPose feedback inside the window. Nav2's own count of behaviour-tree recovery executions, never inferred from /plan or /cmd_vel

cmd_vs_achieved.definition: commanded and achieved velocity resampled onto a 10.0 Hz grid over the window and compared sample by sample. Achieved velocity is a central difference of truth POSE, smoothed over 3 samples: forward speed is the body-frame projection of the xy difference on the heading, angular rate is the wrapped yaw difference. The truth message does carry a twist, but it is a raw 50 Hz finite difference stamped on a different grid and is marked unknown (twist.covariance[0] = -1) whenever two poses share a stamp, so it is not used here. The command series is stamped by the recorder and the truth series by the publisher; the measured offset between the two bases in this stack is under 35 ms, against a 100 ms grid step

speed_vs_target.definition: achieved forward speed on the same 10.0 Hz grid cmd_vs_achieved uses, against 0.46 m/s - the cruise speed this platform is configured with (CRUISE_SPEED/WP_SPEED, recorded in the profile as plant.max_linear_m_s). deficit_fraction is 1 - mean_achieved / target, clamped at 0, so a vehicle at its configured speed reads 0 and a halted one reads 1. after_activation repeats the measurement from the first mobility_fault that reached state=activated to the end of the window, which is the number a mobility fault is read from. ACHIEVED SPEED IS SIMULATOR TRUTH, used here as an evaluation signal: the robot neither measured nor reported it, and no claim is made that it knew it was slow
speed_vs_target.reason: this platform IS commanded in velocity on /cmd_vel; its speed is scored against that command by cmd_vs_achieved rather than against a configured cruise speed

fault_to_response_s.definition: per FaultEvent that reached state=activated: the first MATERIAL change after it. plan_diverged = a /plan leaving the last pre-activation plan by more than max(0.25 m, 1.5x the largest plan-to-plan divergence in this run's pre-activation window); cmd_changed = |linear.x| moving by more than max(0.05 m/s, 1.5x the largest pre-activation excursion), skipped entirely when fewer than two commands precede the activation; recovery_started = Nav2's number_of_recoveries incrementing. Earliest wins, and the trigger is recorded. Both material-change triggers are calibrated against this run's own pre-activation window (10 s sim) and bounded to 2 s sim after activation. At these settings, synthetic activation times swept at 1 s intervals across four fault-free missions still fired cmd_changed on 3 of 38, 5 of 38, 3 of 39 and 3 of 38 instants, and plan_diverged on none of them: a single reported response is weak evidence on its own and must be read beside a control run
fault_to_response_s.reason: no FaultEvent reached state=activated; states seen: none

obstacle_min_clearance_m.definition: smallest (distance from the truth position to the surface of an applied spawned obstacle, minus the footprint radius this robot is scored with) over the interval each obstacle EXISTED - from its activated FaultEvent to its cleared one, or to the end of the mission window. est_error_mean_m.source: /amcl_pose (AMCL (nav2_amcl) over /scan) paired with /ground_truth/odom by header stamp within 50 ms, truth mapped to map by apartment_frames.yaml copied verbatim into env.json

est_error_max_m.source: /amcl_pose (AMCL (nav2_amcl) over /scan) paired with /ground_truth/odom by header stamp within 50 ms, truth mapped to map by apartment_frames.yaml copied verbatim into env.json
est_error_max_m.definition: mean and max |estimate - truth| over the mission window, the estimate being AMCL (nav2_amcl) over /scan; each estimate sample is paired with the nearest truth sample by HEADER stamp, and unpaired samples are dropped rather than matched further out; max over 103 pairs

est_error_at_start_pose_m.source: /amcl_pose (AMCL (nav2_amcl) over /scan) paired with /ground_truth/odom by header stamp within 50 ms, truth mapped to map by apartment_frames.yaml copied verbatim into env.json
est_error_at_start_pose_m.definition: mean |estimate - truth| while the robot is at its start pose and rotating in place: from the first /amcl_pose whose covariance trace is below 0.25 to goal acceptance, excluding any pair whose truth position has already moved more than 0.05 m from the truth position at acceptance. The robot is NOT stationary in this window - AMCL publishes on filter update and its filter updates on motion, so a stopped robot publishes nothing at all; the in-place warm-up rotation leaves xy unchanged, which is what the 0.05 m guard asserts. The guard is applied to the TRUTH half of each pair; within the 50 ms pairing window the body can travel at most 0.023 m, so the bound actually enforced on the estimate half is 0.05 + 0.023 m. It is map error plus world->map alignment error AT THAT ONE POSE, measured, and it is the scale against which in-mission estimate error should be read. It is NOT a lower bound: both terms vary across the map, so in-mission error below this value is normal.; mean over 23 pairs in [19.00, 32.22] s sim

est_pos_horiz_accuracy_max_m.source: none (the profile names no uncertainty topic)

est_pos_horiz_accuracy_max_m.reason: nav2_amcl publishes no ESTIMATOR_STATUS; this platform reports est_cov_trace_max instead

est_status_flags.source: none (the profile names no uncertainty topic)
est_status_flags.definition: fraction of none (the profile names no uncertainty topic) messages inside the mission window in which each ESTIMATOR_STATUS flag was true, plus the message count. The estimator's OWN assessment of which of its states it considers healthy
est_status_flags.reason: nav2_amcl publishes no ESTIMATOR_STATUS; this platform reports its filter health as est_cov_trace_max instead

localization_converged_sim_s.definition: first /amcl_pose whose covariance trace is below 0.25, minus the first /initialpose stamp. AMCL updates its filter on MOTION, so the runner rotates the robot in place while waiting; this measures that wait

collision_count.definition: /bumper messages with a non-empty contacts list inside the window, debounced at 0.5 s sim per colliding pair (gz reports a contact every physics step while two bodies touch); 0 message(s) recorded. A gz contact sensor publishes only on contact, so this zero is a measurement only because the path was shown to be alive in this run: ['ros_gz_bridge'] publishing /bumper, and gz topic /world/ral_apartment/model/ral_roomba/link/base_link/sensor/bumper/contact listed by gz topic -l

plan_publications.definition: count of /plan messages inside the window. This is how often the behaviour tree's RateController (hz=1.0) published a path, NOT a count of replans: the BT republishes at 1 Hz with or without a fault

stopped_time_s.definition: sim seconds inside the window with |linear.x| < 0.01 and |angular.z| < 0.01, zero-order hold on the bag log time (sim), the last command held to the terminal stamp

mission_result.definition: the action status of THIS goal, by UUID, as the server reported it. NavigateToPose's result payload is std_msgs/Empty, so the GoalStatus code is the only verbatim outcome the action offers

recoveries.definition: max number_of_recoveries across NavigateToPose feedback inside the window. Nav2's own count of behaviour-tree recovery executions, never inferred from /plan or /cmd_vel

cmd_vs_achieved.definition: commanded and achieved velocity resampled onto a 10.0 Hz grid over the window and compared sample by sample. Achieved velocity is a central difference of truth POSE, smoothed over 3 samples: forward speed is the body-frame projection of the xy difference on the heading, angular rate is the wrapped yaw difference. The truth message does carry a twist, but it is a raw 50 Hz finite difference stamped on a different grid and is marked unknown (twist.covariance[0] = -1) whenever two poses share a stamp, so it is not used here. The command series is stamped by the recorder and the truth series by the publisher; the measured offset between the two bases in this stack is under 35 ms, against a 100 ms grid step

speed_vs_target.definition: achieved forward speed on the same 10.0 Hz grid cmd_vs_achieved uses, against 0.46 m/s - the cruise speed this platform is configured with (CRUISE_SPEED/WP_SPEED, recorded in the profile as plant.max_linear_m_s). deficit_fraction is 1 - mean_achieved / target, clamped at 0, so a vehicle at its configured speed reads 0 and a halted one reads 1. after_activation repeats the measurement from the first mobility_fault that reached state=activated to the end of the window, which is the number a mobility fault is read from. ACHIEVED SPEED IS SIMULATOR TRUTH, used here as an evaluation signal: the robot neither measured nor reported it, and no claim is made that it knew it was slow
speed_vs_target.reason: this platform IS commanded in velocity on /cmd_vel; its speed is scored against that command by cmd_vs_achieved rather than against a configured cruise speed

fault_to_response_s.definition: per FaultEvent that reached state=activated: the first MATERIAL change after it. plan_diverged = a /plan leaving the last pre-activation plan by more than max(0.25 m, 1.5x the largest plan-to-plan divergence in this run's pre-activation window); cmd_changed = |linear.x| moving by more than max(0.05 m/s, 1.5x the largest pre-activation excursion), skipped entirely when fewer than two commands precede the activation; recovery_started = Nav2's number_of_recoveries incrementing. Earliest wins, and the trigger is recorded. Both material-change triggers are calibrated against this run's own pre-activation window (10 s sim) and bounded to 2 s sim after activation. At these settings, synthetic activation times swept at 1 s intervals across four fault-free missions still fired cmd_changed on 3 of 38, 5 of 38, 3 of 39 and 3 of 38 instants, and plan_diverged on none of them: a single reported response is weak evidence on its own and must be read beside a control run
fault_to_response_s.reason: no FaultEvent reached state=activated; states seen: none

obstacle_min_clearance_m.source: /ground_truth/odom mapped to map by apartment_frames.yaml copied verbatim into env.json, against the spawn_obstacle poses run.json records as applied, converted the same way
obstacle_min_clearance_m.definition: smallest (distance from the truth position to the surface of an applied spawned obstacle, minus the footprint radius this robot is scored with) over the interval each obstacle EXISTED - from its activated FaultEvent to its cleared one, or to the end of the mission window. The obstacle is treated as the oriented rectangle it was spawned as; the footprint as a circle of the radius run.json's pre-flight recorded, falling back to the run's robot profile footprint.radius_m. A negative value is penetration
obstacle_min_clearance_m.reason: no spawn_obstacle intervention was applied in this run

scan_degradation_divergence.definition: /scan compared against /scan_raw beam by beam on IDENTICAL header stamps - the relay republishes the sensor's own header, so an exact stamp key is the only join that compares the same sweep. Two ranges are equal when both are +inf or exactly equal; no tolerance, which would hide the injected noise. pairs_divergent_before_activation must be 0 for "the streams differ only after the fault" to hold, and a non-zero value is the measurement rather than an error. pairs_unmatched and pairs_length_mismatch count the sweeps that were NOT compared - no raw entry at that stamp, or a partner with a different beam count - so the denominator behind pairs_compared is reported rather than hidden; a non-zero count means the relay or the recorder dropped sweeps
